transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I work as a receptionist, and what really pushed me to come in today is... I've been having this issue at work. Every time a door slams, or if someone rolls a suitcase really fast across the lobby, I just jump. 

It feels like it’s happening again. And then it takes me a good minute or so just to get my heart back down to normal. It's just really starting to bother me.
You mentioned 'it feels like it's happening again' — can you tell me what you mean by that? Did something specific happen to you in the past that this reminds you of?

Yeah, um... about two weeks ago, I had a situation at work. A guest got really angry and actually threatened me right there at the front desk. It was pretty intense. 

So when I say it feels like it's happening again, I mean my mind just goes right back to that moment with the guest. This whole jumping at noises thing has been going on for about two weeks, basically ever since he threatened me.

When your mind goes back to that moment with the guest, do you actually feel like you're experiencing it happening right now in that moment, or are you more thinking about the memory of what happened?

Um, I think it's more like a memory, but just a really sudden, strong one. I know I'm still in the present, but out of nowhere I'll just get this clear picture in my head of that guest leaning over the counter and knocking the office equipment toward me. It just pops into my mind, even when I'm just trying to answer a normal phone call.

Since this threatening incident happened two weeks ago, have these intrusive memories and startle reactions been happening continuously the whole time, or did they start a few days after the incident occurred?

It's been pretty much continuous. Like I said, this whole thing has been going on for about two weeks, basically right from the day that guest threatened me at the front desk. It hasn't really let up since then.

Besides the startle reactions and the intrusive memories, have you noticed any other changes in how you're feeling or experiencing things since the incident? For example, do you feel emotionally numb or disconnected from things around you, or have you noticed any gaps in your memory about what happened?

I haven't really noticed any memory gaps, I remember it all pretty clearly. But, um, there is this other thing. Sometimes when I'm back near the front desk, the lobby just feels kind of... distant, I guess? Or unreal for a few seconds. It's almost like I'm watching myself work instead of actually being there and doing it. It's a weird feeling.
Have you been trying to avoid going back to work or staying away from the front desk area where the incident happened?

Yeah, I have. I've actually been taking the back hallway whenever I can. Walking past that specific spot in the lobby where it happened... my chest just tightens up. I just really want to get away from it, so I avoid going through there if I can help it.
You mentioned this has been going on for about two weeks since the incident. Do you expect these symptoms to continue, or do you think they might start getting better on their own soon?

I honestly don't know. I keep hoping I'll just wake up and feel normal going into work again, but... since it hasn't really changed at all in the last two weeks, I'm just not sure what to expect anymore. I'd like to think it'll get better on its own, but right now I really couldn't say. I guess that's kind of why I'm here.

You said the symptoms started right after the incident two weeks ago. But just to be clear — did you start experiencing the jumping, the intrusive memories, and that feeling of things being unreal all on that same day, or did some of these symptoms take a day or two to develop after the threat?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. Um... it's hard to remember if it was that exact same day or maybe the day after. Everything right after the incident was just kind of a blur. I know it all started pretty quickly, but I couldn't tell you for certain if it took a day or two for the jumping and that unreal feeling to actually set in. It all just sort of blended together at first.

When you think back to that day the guest threatened you and the day after, do you remember having any of these symptoms — the jumping at noises, the intrusive memory, or that unreal feeling — on that first day itself, or did they start the next day or a couple days later?

Like I said, I'm really not sure. It's tough to pin down exactly when everything started. That whole first day or two is just really fuzzy for me. I couldn't tell you if the jumping or the memories started that afternoon or the next morning. It just felt like it was all happening at once right around then.

Looking back, between the day the guest threatened you and when you first noticed the jumping at noises or those intrusive memories — was it less than 3 days, or was it more like 3 days or longer before these symptoms really started?

I really couldn't say if it was before or after three days. Um... like I was saying, I just don't have a clear timeline in my head for that first week. It definitely didn't take a long time to start, but whether it was exactly under three days or over, I just don't know for sure.

When you think back to that first day the guest threatened you, did you notice ANY of these symptoms — the jumping at noises, the intrusive memory, or that unreal feeling — happening that same day, or did you first notice them the next day?

I know you're trying to get a specific day, but I honestly just can't separate them in my head. The day it happened and the day after... they're just completely mashed together. I really don't know if I was jumping at noises that very first evening or if it started the next morning. I wish I could give you a clearer timeline, but I just don't have one.

I know the timeline is fuzzy, but let me ask it this way: when you first noticed the jumping at noises or those intrusive memories — was that happening within the first three days after the guest threatened you, or did it start more than three days later?

Look, I really don't mean to keep giving you the same answer, but I just don't know. Like I said, that whole first week is just a blur. It could have been within the first three days, or it could have been on day four... I just can't say for sure. I'm sorry, I just don't have a specific timeframe for when it all kicked in.

The day after the guest threatened you, when you went back to work or were at home that next day — did you notice yourself jumping at sudden noises or having that intrusive memory pop into your head at that time, or did you first start noticing those things later?

I really don't remember what happened that specific next day, whether I was at work or at home. I know you're trying to pin down the exact timing, but... I just don't know if I noticed the jumping or the memories right then, or if it started later on. My memory of those first few days is just completely jumbled. I honestly don't have a better answer for you.

Let me try this a different way. The day you first clearly remember noticing the jumping at noises or having that memory pop into your head — was that within the first 3 days after the guest threatened you, or was it 4 or more days after the incident?

I... I really don't know how else to say it. I just don't know. I can't give you a day. I don't remember when it started clearly enough to say if it was day two, day three, or day four. It's just... it's not there. I'm sorry, I just don't have that answer.

Let me ask it differently. In that first week after the threat, when you were back at work — do you remember being able to do your job normally without jumping at noises, or were you already jumping at sounds right from when you returned to work?

I honestly don't remember going back to work that first week. I mean, I know I must have, but I don't have any clear memory of sitting at the desk or how I was acting. I couldn't tell you if I was doing my job normally or if I was already jumping at every little sound. The whole week is just missing from my head.

Besides not remembering exactly when the symptoms started, are there other parts of that day the guest threatened you or the days right after — like what you did, where you went, or conversations you had — that you just can't remember at all?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I remember the actual incident with the guest pretty clearly. It's not like I have complete blackouts about where I went or who I talked to... it's really just that the whole week after is kind of a blur. So, no, I haven't noticed any other specific things I can't remember, just the timeline of those days.

My profile only states the duration is '2 weeks, ever since that guest threatened me', but does not have specific information about whether there was a symptom-free period right after returning to work or the exact day symptoms started. I have already expressed I cannot remember the exact timing.

patient.answer: I honestly don't remember going back to work that first week. I mean, I know I must have, but I don't have any clear memory of sitting at the desk or how I was acting. I couldn't tell you if I was doing my job normally or if I was already jumping at every little sound. The whole week is just missing from my head.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has dissociative amnesia for the period immediately following the traumatic incident, which would suggest Acute Stress Disorder (F43.01) rather than Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.10 or F43.12). The key diagnostic distinction is that ASD requires dissociative symptoms including amnesia for important aspects of the stressor, while PTSD does not require this. The patient's inability to remember the first week and whether they even went to work is a critical red flag for dissociative amnesia.
doctor.question: Besides not remembering exactly when the symptoms started, are there other parts of that day the guest threatened you or the days right after — like what you did, where you went, or conversations you had — that you just can't remember at all?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about dissociative amnesia (inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event), which is not listed in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, I don't think so. I mean, I remember the actual incident with the guest pretty clearly. It's not like I have complete blackouts about where I went or who I talked to... it's really just that the whole week after is kind of a blur. So, no, I haven't noticed any other specific things I can't remember, just the timeline of those days.

inference.note: Ruled out F43.12 (Prolonged Depressive Reaction). Patient has significant dissociative amnesia regarding the timeline of symptom onset and the first week post-incident, which is characteristic of Acute Stress Disorder (F43.10) rather than a prolonged depressive disorder. The acute onset within days, intrusive memories, hyperarousal (startle reactions), avoidance, and dissociative symptoms (depersonalization and dissociative amnesia) all point to F43.10. The dissociative amnesia about when symptoms started and the entire first week is a key distinguishing feature.

opening_question.question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with acute stress disorder (ASD) following a clearly identified traumatic stressor (threatening incident 2 weeks ago). She demonstrates characteristic ASD symptoms including intrusive memories, exaggerated startle response, avoidance behavior, and dissociative symptoms (derealization/depersonalization). The symptom onset was rapid (within days of the incident), duration is within the 3-day to 1-month window for ASD, and functional impairment is evident at work. While the exact timeline of symptom onset within the first 3 days cannot be definitively established due to the patient's fuzzy recollection of that period, the overall clinical presentation and reported continuous symptomatology since the incident strongly support ASD diagnosis.
